Getting started with knbsdata

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd
library(knbsdata)

knbsdata is a client for official statistics published by the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics. It covers six source families: survey and census study discovery, publications (statistical releases, reports and workbooks, downloadable with verification), census tables as tidy observations, monthly consumer prices from 2009 onwards, the economy as SDMX dataflows (GDP, trade, county finance and 320 more), and geographic reference codes for county-level joins.

Code that contacts the archive is shown but not run here, so building this vignette never depends on a live service.

What is and is not in this version 

knbs_sources()
#> # A tibble: 9 × 8
#>   source_id         source_name  source_type operations stability authentication
#>   <chr>             <chr>        <chr>       <list>     <chr>     <chr>         
#> 1 kenada            Kenya Natio… survey_cat… <chr [4]>  experime… none          
#> 2 finaccess         FinAccess H… static_fil… <chr [1]>  experime… none          
#> 3 knbs_publications KNBS Public… publicatio… <chr [3]>  experime… none          
#> 4 knbs_indicators   KNBS Census… indicator_… <chr [4]>  experime… none          
#> 5 knbs_cpi          KNBS CPI Ex… indicator_… <chr [4]>  experime… none          
#> 6 knbs_opendata     KNBS Data P… indicator_… <chr [3]>  experime… none          
#> 7 opendataforafrica Kenya Open … indicator_… <chr [3]>  experime… none          
#> 8 dhs_program       The DHS Pro… indicator_… <chr [3]>  experime… none          
#> 9 fake_source       Offline tes… fake        <chr [6]>  discovery none          
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: last_verified <date>, base_url <chr>

Eight sources are verified and usable: kenada, the Kenya National Data Archive (surveys); finaccess, the FinAccess portal (open survey microdata); knbs_publications, the KNBS website’s media library; knbs_indicators, the KNBS census data service (2019 census tables, CC BY 4.0); knbs_cpi, the CPI Explorer (monthly consumer prices from 2009); knbs_opendata, the Data Portal (323 SDMX dataflows: GDP, trade, county finance and more); opendataforafrica, the Knoema-operated republisher that fills gaps no first-party portal serves as data — Gross County Product above all; and dhs_program, the DHS Program’s API for the Kenya Demographic and Health Survey indicators, by county from 2014. A source the audit has not verified stays at stability discovery and is never contacted — there is nothing there to call. The source-status vignette says exactly what is and is not covered, and why.

Five ideas worth knowing

1. Everything carries its provenance

Objects returned by the package know where they came from.

meta <- knbs_survey_metadata("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01")
knbs_metadata(meta)

That record holds the source, the retrieval timestamp, the release date, the access conditions and the package version — everything needed to say later what exactly was used.

2. Citations come from the data, not from you 

knbs_cite(meta)
knbs_cite(meta, style = "bibtex")

Where the archive states a required citation, that text is used verbatim and the package adds only the retrieval information. It cannot cite a release the object does not have.

3. Access conditions are data, not decoration

Two different questions, two different columns:

  • access_type is what the archive permits. public_use means public-use files exist.
  • downloadable is what this package will do. For survey microdata it is FALSE throughout; publications, by contrast, are served openly and can be downloaded.

Those differ because the archive requires an account for every download. The package does not automate sign-in, licence acceptance or approval workflows, so knbs_download_microdata() explains the official route and stops. That is a deliberate boundary, not a missing feature.

4. Failure is explicit

Every failure carries a condition class, and none of them return partial data dressed up as a result:

tryCatch(
  knbs_survey_metadata("Kenya"),
  knbs_error_ambiguous_resource = function(cnd) cnd$matches
)

Catch error, or a specific knbs_error_* class — not condition, because httr2 signals a benign condition on every request.

5. Everything is a tibble that speaks tidyverse

Every data-carrying result is a tidy tibble — one row per observation, built on vctrs — so dplyr verbs work directly and keep the provenance attached: filter, mutate, arrange, join, and knbs_metadata() still answers on the result. Aggregations (summarise) and reshapes (pivot_wider) return plain tibbles, because a derived table is your data, not the source’s; tibble::as_tibble() drops the wrapper whenever you want out.

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc") |>                    # Gross County Product
  filter(table_code == "T3", period == 2020) |>
  slice_max(value, n = 5)

knbs_abstract_table("2.2") |>                       # years across, like print
  select(industry, period, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = value)

A first session

Not sure where something lives? Search everything at once — indicators, Statistical Abstract tables, surveys and publications — and each result comes with the call that retrieves it:

hits <- knbs_search("consumer price index")
hits[, c("resource_type", "resource_id", "title", "get")]
#>   resource_type resource_id   title                            get
#> 1 indicator     CPI_ALL_ITEMS Consumer Price Index, all items  knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", source = "knbs_cpi")
#> 2 publication   17052         Kenya-Consumer-Price-Indices-…   knbs_download_publication("17052", destination = ".")
#> ...

eval(parse(text = hits$get[[1]]))   # or copy the call

Words match by stem (“index” finds “Indices”), and CPI, GDP, GCP, KDHS and a few other acronyms are understood both ways. The first search of the day lists the publications library, which takes a few seconds; after that searches are instant.

Or go to one catalogue directly:

# 1. Find something
studies <- knbs_search_surveys("household budget")

# 2. Read its record
meta <- knbs_survey_metadata(studies$survey_id[[1]])

# 3. See what variables it documents
knbs_variables(meta$resource_id, search = "expenditure")

# 4. See what files exist, and on what terms
knbs_survey_files(meta$resource_id)

# 5. Record what you used
knbs_cite(meta)

Publications work the same way, and these files can be downloaded — they are served openly by the KNBS website:

pubs <- knbs_publications("economic survey", year = 2026)
knbs_download_publication(pubs$publication_id[[1]], "data/publications")

The download is verified (a web page arriving where a document was expected is refused), checksummed with SHA-256, and given a <file>.metadata.json provenance sidecar.

Indicators come back as tidy observations — consumer prices, the national accounts, Gross County Product, and census tables with geography down to sub-county:

cpi <- knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", start = "2020-01")
gdp <- knbs_get_indicator("DF_NAT_GDPCP")            # GDP by activity, SDMX
knbs_get_indicator("DF_PF_CG_REV")                   # county govt revenue
gcp <- knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc")                 # Gross County Product

knbs_indicators(topic = "Population")
pop <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001", geo_level = "county")

# The matching reference codes, for census joins
knbs_geographies(level = "county")

Configuration

Options are ordinary R options under the knbsdata. prefix:

knbs_options()
#> $cache
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $cache_dir
#> NULL
#> 
#> $timeout
#> [1] 30
#> 
#> $retries
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $user_agent
#> NULL
#> 
#> $quiet
#> [1] FALSE
knbs_options(timeout = 60, retries = 5)

Caching

Catalogue responses are cached for 24 hours, keyed on the source, the operation, the normalised query and the package’s parser version — so upgrading the package invalidates anything a new parser would read differently.

knbs_cache_info()
knbs_search_surveys("household budget", refresh = TRUE)  # ignore the cache
knbs_cache_clear()

Cached values are checksummed. An entry that fails its checksum is discarded and refetched rather than returned.
